SAS MISSING(numeric-expression | character-expression)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_missing.Rd

1 if the value is missing (blank for character), else 0. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

x

Numeric or character value. A number is missing if it is . or a special missing value (.A to .Z, ._); a character value is missing if it is blank.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Blank character values and special missing values (.A-.Z, ._) are missing; is.na() knows neither.

See also

Other special functions: sas_f_band(), sas_f_blshift(), sas_f_bnot(), sas_f_bor(), sas_f_brshift(), sas_f_bxor(), sas_f_exist(), sas_f_input(), sas_f_inputc(), sas_f_inputn(), sas_f_nvalid(), sas_f_prxchange(), sas_f_prxmatch(), sas_f_prxparse(), sas_f_put(), sas_f_putc(), sas_f_putn()

Examples

# MISSING: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# MISSING returns 1 for the missing value (.).
sas_f_missing(NA_real_)  # missing(.) = 1
#> [1] 1

# Special missing values such as .A also count as missing.
sas_f_missing(sas_missing(".A"))  # missing(.A) = 1
#> [1] 1

# 0 is a valid number, so the result is 0.
sas_f_missing(0)  # missing(0) = 0
#> [1] 0

# For a character argument a blank string counts as missing.
sas_f_missing(" ")  # missing('') = 1
#> [1] 1

# A string with any nonblank character is not missing.
sas_f_missing(" a")  # missing(' a') = 0
#> [1] 0
